printed_page_note: a three-figure printed number stands at the top-left of this exposure, at about x290 y210, and it is not legible: it survives only as a blurred offset, and neither the exposure's own sense nor its mirror resolves to figures that can be told apart. It is recorded as unknown rather than guessed, and NOT inferred from the sorted filename order, which is not the book order. 33S7-9YYJ-B1 and 33S7-9YYJ-8D are recorded the same way for the same reason.
division_note: the printed heading reads `by the Marshal of the ____ District (or Territory) of` with `Illinois` written into the blank in the enumerator's hand and the district blank left unfilled. No enumerator's name is written on the exposure, so no division is recorded; 33S7-9YYJ-5D carries `S. W. Sherman` and this sheet does not, and it is not carried over from a neighbouring image.
line_count_note:
coverage.json inventoried this image at 31 lines `to the nearest line`. Read line by line it carries 30 entries, on a grid whose first writing line stands at y659 and whose thirtieth at y2868 — pitch 76.1 px over the 29 intervals. The body is ruled VERTICALLY ONLY: a horizontal-rule profile taken through the three blocks that carry no writing (the slaves block, the pensioners block, and the deaf/blind/insane and schools blocks) finds a rule at y585 and another at y3018 and NOTHING between them, so the row of a number cannot be counted off the form and has to be fitted to the ink.

The grid was fitted to the INDUSTRY columns' own ink — the columns that close against their printed footings — and the TOTAL column was then read against it rather than used to build it, so the row index and the numbers are independent. `tools/fit_census_line_grid.py` on the 25 industry anchors alone answers 30 lines at rms 6.17, pitch 75.87, against 15.12 for the next-best line count and 18.52 for the one below — a factor of two and a half either way; and under `--jackknife` 23 of the 25 single-anchor drops still choose 30, so the count does not rest on one entry. Run over the committed anchors of every column the same tool answers 30 lines at rms 5.18, pitch 76.12 (5.63 under `--ink-line`), against 14.80 or worse for 31 through 38.

The body between the two rules is 2433 px, which at this pitch leaves room for a thirty-first line at about y2944 and for a line above the first at about y583; both are blank in every one of the sheet's 37 columns. The inventory count is superseded by this reading.
form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. The printed headings were read off this exposure itself, rotated upright: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL — number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (names, ages); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns.
geometry_note: the leaf is skewed on the exposure the OPPOSITE way to 33S7-9YYJ-B1's: the printed vertical rules of the industry block drift about 20 px to the LEFT between y=620 and y=2900, a slope of -0.00932 px per px of y, taken as the mean of nine rules each fitted x = m*y + c over eight bands down the page (individual slopes -0.0082 to -0.0113). The reading was made against a sheared copy (x' = x - slope*(y-620) = x + 0.00932*(y-620), y untouched), on which the rules bounding the TOTAL and industry columns stand at x = 1294, 1489, 1555, 1619, 1684, 1765, 1845, 1926 and 1991 at every height to within 3 px, and the eighteen rules of the deaf/blind/insane and schools blocks at 2432, 2512, 2590, 2667, 2746, 2827, 2908, 2997, 3077, 3157, 3248, 3333, 3401, 3466, 3532, 3612, 3672 and 3736. Every x quoted in this file is an x on that sheared copy; every y is an y of the exposure itself, because a horizontal shear leaves y alone. `column_closure.*.entry_boxes` are the exception and are stated in the EXPOSURE's own coordinates, because `fit_census_line_grid.py --ink-line` re-measures inside them against the raw image. The de-sheared column map is B1's own, offset a uniform +36 px: 1258/1453/1519/1583/1648/1729/1809/1890/1955 there against 1294/1489/1555/1619/1684/1765/1845/1926/1991 here, the column widths agreeing to 2 px throughout. That is the printed form, and the ticket's advice to start from B1's geometry held.
tool_note: tools/read_census_continuation.py still does not run on this image: 33S7-9YYJ-B2 is one of the four its rule finder exits on with `no industry run bracketed by TOTAL and PENSIONERS`, for the skew recorded above. The reading here was made at magnification against a measured, sheared column map, on the same basis as 33S7-9YYJ-8D and 33S7-9YYJ-B1. The tool is not weakened to fit.
right_edge_note: unlike 33S7-9YYJ-B1, this exposure's right edge is legible past the last recorded column: the seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns end at x3736 and the form's final column — white persons over 20 years of age who cannot read and write, x3736 to about x3810 — is visible on every line and carries nothing written. The leaf goes into the gutter and to black beyond about x3820 (the median brightness of a 30-px band falls from 108 at x3790 to 2 at x3820), but that is past the printed table. The final column is NOT among the 37 this schema records, which is 33S7-9YYJ-8D's and B1's shape and is kept; that it is legible and empty here is recorded in this note instead of by adding a thirty-eighth field.
closure_note: The enumerator added his own totals at the foot of the sheet. Those totals are transcribed under `footer_as_read` and every column carrying a figure is checked against them in `column_closure`. A column that does not close keeps its residual and its reading is NOT adjusted to make the total come out — the residual is the finding.

footer_as_read.footer_blank_columns_note: the slaves block, mining, agriculture, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, the pensioners block, every deaf/dumb/blind/insane column white and coloured, and every schools column carry no figure at the foot of this sheet and no entry on any of its 30 lines. The right-hand half of the footer strip, x2400 to x3800, was read at magnification and is blank across its whole width.
footer_as_read.footer_total_glyph_note: the TOTAL footing is three figures. The first two are a pair of thin ascending slashes of equal length and weight, their feet about 25 px apart with no hook or base stroke on either — this hand's 11, on T-0643's finding that it writes 11 as two strokes about 30 px apart and 1 as one stroke, and NOT its 4, which is a matched pair with the second stroke set below and touching the first (lines 11, 14 and 21 of this sheet write that). The third figure carries the top bar drawn to the right and the heavy descender curling left that this hand puts on every 5 (lines 1, 29 and 30 write the same glyph). Read 115, and the line-by-line sum of the column is 115 exactly.
footer_as_read.footer_industry_glyph_note: the commerce footing is a slash and a 2 — 12; the manufactures and trades footing is a slash and a 7 — 17; the learned professions footing is a single 2. Two nearly-vertical strokes inside those figures register as vertical rules on a profile taken through the footer band (at de-sheared x1413 and x1728) and are the enumerator's own ink, not printed rules: neither appears anywhere in the body.

closes_note:
THREE of the four columns that carry a figure close EXACTLY, and the fourth is one person over.

THE FAMILY TOTALS READ 115 AGAINST A PRINTED 115. That is the first continuation sheet in this deposit whose TOTAL column closes on the nose (33S7-9YYJ-B1 is -1, 33S7-9YYJ-5D +3, 33S7-9YYJ-8D +15, 33S7-9YYJ-6Q -25), and nothing was re-read after the sum was known to make it happen: the thirty line values were committed off the glyphs, then added. It is worth saying what the close is evidence FOR, because on an unruled sheet the line count and the numbers are usually entangled. Here they are not. The grid was fitted to the industry columns' ink; the TOTAL column was read against it; and the sum of the TOTAL column then matched the enumerator's own footing. A wrong line count would have had to drop or invent a value and still come to 115.

MANUFACTURES AND TRADES READS 17 AGAINST A PRINTED 17. Ten of its thirteen entries are the plain tapered ascending slash this hand writes for 1. Line 18 carries a 5 — the top bar drawn right and the heavy descender curling left into a bottom-left loop, the same glyph as the TOTAL column's line 1, line 29 and line 30, and as the footing's own third figure. That leaves lines 24 and 26, and they are the two readings on this sheet that do not rest on the glyph alone; see `manufactures_doubtful_cells`.

LEARNED PROFESSIONS AND ENGINEERS READS 2 AGAINST A PRINTED 2, on lines 2 and 5, both plain slashes. A third faint diagonal wisp stands in the same column at y1028, between lines 5 and 6 and on neither; it has no pen taper and is read as a crease, not a figure.

COMMERCE READS 13 AGAINST A PRINTED 12, a residual of +1, and it is left standing. Thirteen lines carry a mark in that column and every one of them is the same plain ascending slash as the ten in the manufactures column; none is faint, none is doubtful in position, and every one falls on a line the grid already had. The nearest thing to a candidate for the odd one out is line 18 at y1940, whose slash is drawn with the pen doubling back so that it encloses a narrow loop — but a doubled stroke is still a stroke, and dropping it because the column would then close is exactly the move this file is written not to make. Which of the thirteen the enumerator did not count, or whether he simply mis-added, cannot be said from this sheet.

MINING, AGRICULTURE, NAVIGATION OF THE OCEAN AND NAVIGATION OF CANALS, LAKES AND RIVERS are empty at the foot and empty on every line. One mark sits in the canal-navigation column, at y2364: a small round blot about 12 px across with no stroke direction and no pen taper, and — the point — it falls 38 px below line 23 and 35 px above line 24, on NEITHER writing line, where every one of the 58 entries this sheet does commit falls on one. It is read as a blot rather than a figure, and that is a reading made on the mark's own shape and position, not on the footer: 33S7-9YYJ-B1's disputed canal mark was committed as a 1 with a +1 residual left standing precisely because it DID sit on a line.

line_24.what_is_there: a bold, long, tapered ascending slash — this hand's 1 — with a second stroke beside it that is thinner, shorter and markedly lighter in tone, the two overlapping in y rather than standing foot to foot.
line_24.why_1: the light stroke has neither the weight nor the taper of the bold one beside it and reads as offset transfer from the facing leaf, of which this exposure carries a good deal (a mirrored three-figure number at the top-left corner, and mirrored heading type along the right edge). Read as two figures the cell would be 11, and line 24's own family total is 2 — the form's column is `number of persons in EACH FAMILY employed in`, so the cell cannot exceed the total beside it. Both of those are readings off the sheet, not off the footing.
line_24.what_would_change: if the light stroke is ink, the cell is 11, the column reads 27 against a printed 17, and no line-24 family of 2 can hold it.

line_26.what_is_there: a heavily inked closed loop about 50 px across with a horizontal stroke crossing to the right of it and a small second loop at the bottom left. It is NOT the plain slash this hand writes for 1, and this file says so rather than pretending otherwise.
line_26.why_1: line 26's family total is 2 and its commerce cell is 1, so at most one person of that family is left to stand in manufactures. That is the sheet's own arithmetic on two independently committed columns, one of which (TOTAL) closes exactly against the enumerator's footing. Taken on its form alone the glyph would read as a 4 or an 8; taken with the line it stands on it can only be 1, drawn over a blot or with the pen doubling back on itself. The column then also closes at 17, which is corroboration and was NOT the ground of the decision — the family total was.
line_26.what_would_change: read as its apparent loop-form (4) the column reads 20 against a printed 17, and line 26 puts 5 of a 2-person family into trade.

manufactures_doubtful_cells.note: these are the only two cells on the sheet committed on anything other than the glyph in front of them. Every other one of the 58 entries is read off its own ink.

pairing.why: a continuation sheet carries no name, and this one's printed page number is illegible, so the pairing to its left sheet is a separate reading: the page population below has to be matched against the printed age-band totals at the foot of each candidate left sheet. T-0642 does that for all eleven at once. Recorded as unpaired rather than guessed. What T-0642 lacked for this sheet — a population key — it now has.
pairing.page_population_key_note: the printed footer figure, which is what a left sheet's age-band sums are to be matched against. The line-by-line reading of the same column is 115 as well, so on this sheet the two keys are one number and the pairing test has no slack to allow for.

largest_household_key.note: a 14-person household is the strongest single signal here: the left sheet that belongs to this one must carry, on its eighteenth line, a name with about fourteen people distributed across its age bands, and six of them at work — one in commerce and five in manufactures and trades. On an 1840 Chicago sheet that is a shop or a small works with its hands living in.

household_shape_key.note: this sheet's second signal is the shape of the whole column rather than one big house: thirty families summing to 115, a mean of 3.83, with eleven of the thirty holding one or two people and only three holding more than seven (lines 4 and 16 at 11 and line 18 at 14). A left sheet whose age-band rows sum to 115 across 30 lines but distribute them evenly is the wrong partner.

employment_key.note: 32 of the 115 persons on this sheet are returned as employed, and every one of them in commerce, in manufactures and trades, or in the learned professions — not one in agriculture, and not one in navigation of any kind. For an 1840 Cook County sheet that is a town street, not a farming township, and it is a strong constraint on which left sheet can belong to it.

digit_key_used.from: 33S7-9YYJ-B1.json § digit_key_used and § footer_total_glyph_note, itself resting on 33S7-9YYJ-6Q's key from the labelled exemplar 33S7-9YYJ-24, plus T-0643's stroke-count finding on 33S7-9YYJ-8D
digit_key_used.why: the two forms that decide a continuation sheet's arithmetic are the pair of slashes (11 or 4) and the loop-and-bar family (3, 5 or 6). Both are settled on this sheet by the sheet itself: it has three unambiguous matched pairs where the second stroke sits below and TOUCHING the first (lines 11, 14 and 21) and two unambiguous separated pairs of equal strokes about 25 px apart (lines 4 and 16), and the two shapes are plainly different at 6x. Committing the touching form as 4 and the separated form as 11 makes the column sum to the enumerator's own 115 exactly. Committing them the other way round makes it 136, and committing both as 4 makes it 101.

forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.1: one bold tapered ascending slash — lines 7, 8, 12, 13, 17, 20, 28, and ten of the thirteen manufactures entries and all thirteen commerce entries
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.2: one continuous path: an upper stroke rising to the right, then down and back left into a base stroke that ends in a blob at its LEFT end. Lines 5, 6, 23, 24, 25, 26 and 27 — seven of them, which is what makes this the best-attested form on the sheet. It is the form most easily mistaken for a pair of slashes, and the left-hand hook on the lower stroke is what tells them apart.
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.3: a curl over a loop in one stroke, the upper part angular — lines 3, 9, 10 and 19
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.4: the matched pair, upper stroke bold and long, second shorter and set below and touching — lines 11, 14 and 21
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.5: the bar drawn right at the top with a rising tail, the heavy descender curling left into a bottom-left loop — lines 1, 29, 30, the manufactures entry on line 18, and the footing's third figure
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.6: a slanted closed oval with a tail rising to the upper right — lines 2 and 22
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.7: a short top stroke with a hook at its left, then a long descender falling to the lower left — line 15
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.11: two thin ascending slashes of equal length and weight, feet about 25 px apart, neither hooked — lines 4 and 16, and the first two figures of the footing
forms_confirmed_on_this_sheet.14: three strokes: the 1 followed by the 4's matched pair — line 18

digit_key_used.not_in_the_key: 8, 9 and 0 do not occur on this sheet in any cell, and nothing here is read as one.
